questions.question: Define open dumping.
questions.solution_html:
• Define open dumping. /

  • where waste is simply thrown onto land or into water bodies without any proper treatment,
  • management, or environmental protection measures. (2marks)

  • fertility, structure, and water-holding capacity. (2 marks)

questions.question: Explain in detail about end products of composting.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain in detail the end products of composting. /
  • Humus (finished compost) – A dark, crumbly, soil-like material rich in nutrients; improves soil fertility,
  • structure, and water-holding capacity. Carbon dioxide (CO₂) – Released during microbial respiration.
  • Water (H₂O) – Produced during decomposition and helps maintain moisture. Heat – Generated due
  • to microbial activity, which aids in pathogen destruction. Mineral nutrients – Such as nitrogen,
  • phosphorus, potassium, and trace elements in forms available to plants.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: phosphorus, potassium, and trace elements in forms available to plants.

questions.question: Describe about the advantages and disadvantages of composting.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the advantages and disadvantages of composting. /
  • Advantages: Reduces waste volume and decreases landfill burden , Produces nutrient-rich compost
  • that improves soil fertility, Environment-friendly – reduces pollution and greenhouse gas emissions,
  • Improves soil structure and water-holding capacity, Recycles organic waste into useful material, Low-
  • cost and simple method for waste management, Reduces need for chemical fertilisers.
  • Disadvantages: Slow process – takes weeks to months, requires proper maintenance (moisture,
  • aeration, temperature), may produce foul odour if not managed properly. Attracts pests and insects,
  • requires space for a composting setup, Not suitable for all types of waste (e.g., plastics, metals).
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: requires space for a composting setup, Not suitable for all types of waste (e.g., plastics, metals).
